pass_a_gloss: [...] would become impious daring deeds. He calls to witness then very fittingly both heaven and earth? For since he was about to make the blames against Israel, he wishes both the angels in heaven, and the whole earth itself, to know the ways of that one's impiety, so that no one may think that [God] was moved in vain, or rashly, upon small and very cheap faults, to make cast off the beloved, and the people set for his lot, and the one rescued of old through very much strength from the greed of the Egyptians. For he pitied [them] as wronged beyond the likely, and the nobility fitting and being in the fathers, burdened by an unwilled servitude. And since those who wronged were acting against, they were punished bitterly, God throwing upon them every manner of torment. Just as then most conspicuous became the taking up of those from Israel, thus he wishes also the manner of the casting off not to be unknown. And if some should wish that the elements themselves too are called through the voice of the prophet, the force of the thoughts would not miss the fitting sense, for those who have considered that. For Israel was being redeemed, as I said, from the unholiness of the Egyptians through Moses. But since Pharaoh, unholily rising against the nods of God, was saying: I do not know the Lord, and Israel I will not send away, the creation armed itself together with its own master against those who were hostile. For from above and from heaven very many and conspicuous signs came to be, and very many likewise and not unwonderful in the earth itself. For the heaven sent down the hail, and the earth threw out frogs, as it is written; and the water was changed into blood, and soot of furnace being scattered, and muddying the air, sores and blisters boiling up happened upon the bodies of all. As then the elements themselves had all but laboured in vain over those redeemed, Hear, heaven, he says, and give ear, earth, because the Lord spoke. And we will approach also otherwise the thoughts of the things set before us. For those from Israel, having dishonoured the training through law, and having neglected the saving lessons, having left the one and by nature God, were bringing the services to the unclean demons on mountains and hills, and in the most wooded ravines they burned incense and worshipped the works of their own hands. And the God of all was vexed at these things, and very fittingly, and said to one of the holy prophets: Rise up and be judged toward the mountains, and let the hills hear your voice. Hear, hills, the judgment of the Lord, and the ravines, foundations of the earth, because a judgment is to the Lord toward the p[eople] [the section breaks off].
pass_b_english: He has very good reason, then, to call heaven and earth to witness. He was about to bring charges against Israel, and he wants the angels in heaven, and the whole earth itself, to know the ways of that people's impiety, so that no one would think that God had been moved without cause, or had rushed, over small and quite trivial faults, to cast off the beloved, the people set apart as His own portion, whom long ago He had rescued with very great strength from the greed of the Egyptians.

For He had mercy on them as a people wronged beyond all reason, weighed down by an unwilling servitude, contrary to the nobility that befitted their fathers and was native to them. And when their oppressors resisted, they were bitterly punished, as God hurled every kind of torment upon them. So, just as Israel's being taken up as His own was most conspicuous, He wants the manner of their casting off not to go unknown either.

If some would rather take it that the elements themselves are being called by the prophet's voice, the force of the thought would not miss the fitting sense, for those who have considered the following. Israel, as I said, was being redeemed through Moses from the ungodliness of the Egyptians. But when Pharaoh, impiously rising up against the commands of God, said, “I do not know the Lord, and I will not let Israel go” (Exodus 5:2), creation armed itself with its own Master against those who were hostile. From above, from heaven, came a great many striking signs, and likewise a great many wonders on the earth itself. Heaven sent down hail (Exodus 9:23), and the earth threw up frogs, as it is written (Exodus 8:6); the water was changed into blood (Exodus 7:20); and when furnace soot was scattered and clouded the air, sores and blisters broke out on the bodies of everyone (Exodus 9:8–10). So, since the very elements had all but laboured in vain over those who had been redeemed, he says: “Hear, O heaven, and give ear, O earth, for the Lord has spoken” (Isaiah 1:2).

But let us approach the sense of the passage in another way as well. Those of Israel dishonoured the training given through the Law and neglected the saving teachings; they forsook the one God, who is God by nature, and brought their worship to unclean demons on mountains and hills, and in the most thickly wooded ravines they burned incense to the works of their own hands and bowed down to them. The God of all was angered at this, and with very good reason, and He said to one of the holy prophets: “Arise, plead your case before the mountains, and let the hills hear your voice. Hear, O hills, the judgment of the Lord, and you ravines, foundations of the earth, for the Lord has a judgment against His p…” (Micah 6:1–2).

choices.why: The section continues Logos 1; no new question is invented before it.
rejected: How could God tolerate the wicked deeds of Israel?

choices.why: προαλής, rash; God did not cast off Israel hastily over small faults.
θητεία, hired labour; Israel's forced labour in Egypt.
The sores and blisters rose on all bodies (Exodus 9:8-10); the clause is kept whole.

choices.english: creation armed itself with its own Master
choices.why: Creation fights on God's side against Egypt's hostility.
